arguments.spec:
# Refactor: Replace the Notification-Routing Conditional Thicket

`src/notifications.mjs`'s `routeNotification` is one function holding four event kinds, each with its own
channel-preference order and reason text -- a new kind or channel means another branch in the same body.
`src/audit.mjs` carries a byte-identical copy of the reachability computation, so the router and the audit can
silently drift apart. Restructure the code; do not change a single routing decision. `src/index.mjs` must keep
exporting `routeNotification`, `routeAll`, `CHANNELS` and `auditRoutability` by those exact names.

The behaviour, stated precisely (frozen scenarios own these, read them before touching anything):
- A result is always `{ channel, reason, subscriberId, reachableSummary }`; `channel` is `null` when nothing is
  chosen, `reason` always explains why, verbatim strings matter.
- Reachable channels, fixed precedence: `sms` (phone AND verified), `push` (pushToken), `webhook` (webhookUrl),
  `email` (email). `reachableSummary` joins them with `|`, or is the string `none`.
- Quiet hours suppress `mention` and `digest` only -- NOT `security_alert` or `billing`.
- Preference per kind: `security_alert` -> sms, then email. `billing` -> email only. `mention` -> push, then
  email. `digest` -> webhook, then email. First reachable channel in that order wins.
- An unknown kind routes nowhere, reason names the kind. Missing/kind-less event or missing/id-less subscriber
  throws `TypeError`.

`scenarios/`, `test/refactor.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every
run. Two things are measured every run: BEHAVIOUR (all 9 frozen scenarios B01-B09 must keep passing exactly as
before) and STRUCTURE, graded against exactly three goals in `refactor/manifest.json`'s `refactor/goals.json`:

- G1 `max_branches_per_function` (limit 6) -- counted as if/case/ternary/&&/||/catch. Verified against the real
  fixture: the unmodified `routeNotification` has far more than 6.
- G2 `max_function_lines` (limit 25). Verified against the real fixture: the unmodified `routeNotification` is
  well over 25 meaningful lines.
- G3 `no_duplicate_block` (windowLines 5) -- no 5 substantive source lines may appear in two different files
  under `src/`. Verified against the real fixture: the unmodified tree fails this now (the reachability block
  is byte-identical between `src/notifications.mjs` and `src/audit.mjs`).

The deliverable is `refactor/manifest.json`: `addressed` lists the goal ids genuinely met; every goal you list
is checked immediately and strictly. `complete: true` requires every goal listed and met. `npm test` must pass
exactly as-is, offline -- never add a dependency.

One repair, hand-verified against the real fixture in a scratch copy to satisfy all three goals at once while
leaving all 9 frozen behaviour scenarios passing unchanged (14/14 total, including with `complete: true`): every
channel-reachability check the routing logic uses is IDENTICAL to the general reachability predicate already
computed for `reachableSummary` (e.g. security_alert's sms condition `phone && verified` is exactly reachable's
sms condition) -- so routing can become a lookup over precomputed `reachable` channels instead of re-testing the
subscriber. Extract: `src/reachability.mjs` (the shared reachable-channels + summary computation, used by both
the router and the audit -- this is what removes the G3 duplication), `src/validation.mjs` (the shared event/
subscriber checks), `src/routingRules.mjs` (a per-kind data table -- precedence order, reasons, quiet-hours
suppression -- plus one small generic `decideChannel` engine that walks it). `notifications.mjs` and `audit.mjs`
both shrink to a few lines each that just call the shared pieces; `index.mjs` needs no change since the four
exported names stay in their current files.
arguments.plan:
Two cards, chained:

1. `extract-routing-rules-and-shared-reachability` -- does the actual restructuring: new src/reachability.mjs,
   src/validation.mjs, src/routingRules.mjs; src/notifications.mjs and src/audit.mjs rewritten to compose them.
   Verified empirically against the real fixture: all 9 behaviour scenarios (B01-B09) still pass, and claiming
   G1+G2+G3 against the refactored tree is genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier (no function over 6
   branches, no function over 25 meaningful lines, no 5-line duplicate block anywhere under src/). This card
   lists all three goals in refactor/manifest.json's `addressed` (leaving `complete: false`) once it has
   verified them itself via a real npm test run in-session.
2. `verify-and-complete-notification-routing-refactor` (depends on 1) -- independently re-verifies (does not
   trust the previous card) that all three goals are genuinely met via a fresh npm test run, then sets
   `complete: true`.
arguments.summary: src/notifications.mjs's routeNotification is one function with a branch per event-kind-times-channel combination, and src/audit.mjs duplicates its reachability computation verbatim. Plan: one card extracts the shared reachability check, the shared validation, and a per-kind precedence/reason data table (walked by one small generic decideChannel engine) into three new modules, shrinking notifications.mjs and audit.mjs to thin composers -- verified empirically against the real fixture to satisfy all three structural goals at once while keeping all 9 frozen behaviour scenarios passing exactly as before (14/14 including complete:true); one card independently re-verifies and marks the manifest complete. No open assumptions.

tasks.title: Extract shared reachability/validation and a per-kind routing-rules table
tasks.prompt:
Restructure src/ so routeNotification stops being a single branch-per-kind function, and the
reachability computation stops being duplicated between notifications.mjs and audit.mjs.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture, not assumed): claiming G1+G2+G3 against the UNMODIFIED tree fails
all three -- routeNotification has far more than 6 branch points and far more than 25 meaningful lines, and the
4-line reachability block (`if (subscriber.phone && subscriber.verified === true) reachable.push("sms"); ...`)
is byte-identical in src/notifications.mjs and src/audit.mjs.

Read the behaviour section of specification.md and scenarios/routing.scenarios.mjs (B01-B09) before writing
anything -- the precedence and quiet-hours rules are subtle (an unverified phone does not count as sms-reachable;
quiet hours suppress mention/digest only) and must be reproduced exactly, not re-derived from what the current
code looks like it does.

Shape (verified empirically against the real fixture: all 9 frozen behaviour scenarios B01-B09 keep passing
exactly as before, and G1+G2+G3 are all genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier, including with
`complete: true`):

- New `src/reachability.mjs` exporting `reachableChannelsFor(subscriber)` (the existing 4-line reachable-array
  computation, moved here UNCHANGED, returning the array) and `reachableSummaryFor(reachable)` (the existing
  `reachable.join("|") || "none"`, moved here UNCHANGED). This is the ONE place the reachability rule lives --
  both the router and the audit call it, which is what makes G3 pass and is what makes them structurally unable
  to disagree.
- New `src/validation.mjs` exporting `validateEvent(event)` and `validateSubscriber(subscriber)` -- the
  existing two guard clauses (throwing the same TypeErrors with the same messages), moved here UNCHANGED.
- New `src/routingRules.mjs` exporting `decideChannel(kind, quiet, reachable)`. Internally, a module-level data
  table keyed by event kind holds each kind's ordered channel precedence (as `{ channel, reason }` pairs), an
  optional quiet-hours suppression reason (present only for `mention` and `digest`), and a `noneReason` for when
  nothing is reachable. `decideChannel` looks up the kind's rule (returns `{ channel: null, reason: "unknown
  event kind <kind>" }` if there is none), returns the quiet-hours reason immediately if `quiet` is true and the
  rule has one, otherwise walks the precedence list and returns the first `{ channel, reason }` whose channel is
  in the `reachable` array, falling back to `{ channel: null, reason: noneReason }`. Every routing decision
  (which channel wins, which reason string) must come out byte-identical to today for every input the scenarios
  exercise -- this table is a direct transcription of the five kind-specific branches, not a redesign of them.
- `src/notifications.mjs`: keep exporting `CHANNELS` (unchanged array) and `routeAll` (unchanged body).
  `routeNotification` becomes: validate the event and subscriber (via validation.mjs), compute `reachable` and
  `reachableSummary` (via reachability.mjs), call `decideChannel(event.kind, subscriber.quietHours === true,
  reachable)`, and assemble the same four-field result object as before.
- `src/audit.mjs`: `auditRoutability` becomes: validate the subscriber (via validation.mjs, replacing its own
  inline check), compute `reachable`/`reachableSummary` (via reachability.mjs), and assemble the same
  three-field result as before.
- `src/index.mjs`: no change needed -- all four exported names stay in the same files they are already
  re-exported from.

Do not change any reason string, precedence order, or the quiet-hours kind list. Never add a dependency (the
sandbox is offline).

fresh. (2) In a later turn, write the three new modules and rewrite notifications.mjs and audit.mjs
(write_file for whole-file rewrites; do not retry an identical rejected edit_file call more than once -- fall
back to write_file). (3) In a further later turn, run npm test and confirm every one of the 9 behaviour
